'''Leon Powe Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|p|oʊ}}; born January 22, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Drafted in [[2006 NBA Draft|2006]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]], Powe grew up in [[Oakland, California]], and played [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]]. He played his first three years in the NBA with the [[Boston Celtics]] and won a championship with the team in [[2008 NBA Finals|2008]]. From 2009 to 2011, Powe played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He also had a stint with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2011. After a stint in Puerto Rico, Powe announced his retirement in 2014 citing multiple injuries and his desire to become a businessman.

==Early life==
Powe grew up in Oakland, California. His father left him when he was two years old. When he was seven years old, the family's house burned down and they were homeless for years. They moved more than twenty times within six years. He and his siblings were taken away from their mother by the state of California and put into [[foster care]]. Powe's mother died four days before he played in the state championship.<ref name="Express">{{cite web|last=Hubbard|first=Lee|title=The Making of Leon Powe |url=http://www.eastbayexpress.com/gyrobase/the-making-of-leon-powe/Content?oid=1069363&showFullText=true|work=East Bay Express|date=February 19, 2003}}</ref>

==High school career==
Powe attended [[Oakland Technical High School]] along with former [[Seattle Seahawks]] running back [[Marshawn Lynch]], where he averaged 27.4 [[Points per game|ppg]], 14.2 [[Rebounds per game|rpg]] and 3.1 [[Block (basketball)|bpg]] as a senior. With Powe in the roster, Oakland Tech won the CIF Oakland Section Championship and also reached the CIF State Championships in 2002 and 2003. He was named a first-team Parade All-American and the Gatorade California Player of the Year during his senior year. A highly rated prep star, Powe was selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American]] game and became the first Oakland Tech athlete to have his number retired by the school.<ref>[http://calbears.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/powe_leon00.html Player Bio: Leon Powe :: Men's Basketball<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060614183837/http://calbears.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/powe_leon00.html |date=June 14, 2006 }}</ref>

==College career==
Powe played [[college basketball]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Golden Bears]] from 2003 to 2006. Although he was present for three seasons, he did not play in his sophomore year (2004–05) due to a serious knee injury.<ref name=testdraft>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2414186 Cal sophomore Powe to test draft - NBA - ESPN]</ref> During his freshman season, he was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]], leading the conference in rebounding.

Questions abounded about whether Powe would return to form following his knee surgery, but he worked hard and rehabilitated to become a dominant force on the interior as he continued to improve his game. He produced 20.5 PPG and 10.1 RPG while leading Cal to a 20–11 record and a berth in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]].

Powe was named California's most valuable player during a banquet in April 2006. Powe, who also was selected Cal's [[Most valuable player|MVP]] as a [[freshman]] in 2004, averaged 20.5 ppg and 10.1 rpg to become just the sixth player ever to pace the [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10 Conference]] in both categories. Named a second-team [[All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]], the U.S. Basketball Writers and [[ESPN.com]], he was chosen to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]] for a second time in 2006.

==Professional career==
After his junior year, Powe decided to enter his name in the [[2006 NBA draft]].<ref name=testdraft/> Powe was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the second round as the 49th overall pick. The Nuggets subsequently traded him to the [[Boston Celtics]]. After playing for the Celtics summer league team, Powe was signed by the team to a 3-year contract.  Although Powe did not reach the sum of 14 in his per game points, rebounds, and assists necessary to guarantee the second year of his contract, that second year became guaranteed when Boston did not waive him by July 1, 2007.  Powe had a similar hurdle of 16 for the sum of the three statistics to guarantee the third year of his contract ([[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]]).<ref>{{cite news|last=Okanes|first=Jonathan|title=Celtics put Cal's Powe on payroll|url=http://www.contracostatimes.com/mld/cctimes/sports/colleges/cal/15071722.htm|newspaper=Contra Costa Times|date=July 19, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061208090142/http://www.contracostatimes.com/mld/cctimes/sports/colleges/cal/15071722.htm|archive-date=December 8, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/articles/2006/08/06/blazers_coach_plays_defense/ | work=The Boston Globe | title=Blazers coach plays defense | date=August 6, 2006 | first=Peter | last=May}}</ref>

===2006–07 NBA season===
Powe played as a fourth string center behind [[Kendrick Perkins]], [[Brian Scalabrine]] and [[Michael Olowokandi]] in his rookie season. After a rash of injuries submarined Boston's playoff chances, Powe received a limited opportunity to showcase his skills. He proved himself a capable defender who could alter shots and provide interior [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]]. On January 12, 2007, Powe made the most out of his 25 minutes and registered a career-high 12 rebounds against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. On April 10, 2007, he scored  19 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Powe finished the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 campaign]] averaging 4.2 points and 3.4 rebounds in just over 11 minutes per game.

===2007–08 NBA season===
[[Image:Leon Powe Free Throw.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Powe shoots a [[free throw]] in Game 4 of the [[2008 NBA Playoffs]] against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].]]
[[File:2008-04-17 celtics 01web (Leon Powe).jpg|thumb|Powe at an event during the 2007–08 season]]

On January 29, 2008, Powe had a breakout performance that took place in [[Miami]] against the [[Miami Heat|Heat]], as he effectively filled in the blank of the absent main contributors [[Kevin Garnett]] and [[Ray Allen]], scoring 25 [[point (basketball)|points]] and grabbing 11 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] en route to a 117–87 blowout victory.<ref>Steve Bulpett, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1069948 Celtics elect to win], ''Boston Herald'', January 30, 2008.</ref> He also scored his career-high 27 points in the last game of the season against the [[New Jersey Nets]] on April 16, 2008.<ref>Mark Murphy, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1087748&srvc=celt&position=6 C's go through motions, gear up for postseason], ''Boston Herald'', April 17, 2008.</ref>

One of his most notable performances of the season came in [[2008 NBA Finals#Game 2|Game 2]] of the [[2008 NBA Finals]] against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on June 8, 2008, as he scored 21 [[Point (basketball)|points]],  which included several dunks and 13 free throw attempts in only 15 minutes of play in front of a crowd chanting his name<ref>Chris Forsberg, [https://web.archive.org/web/20121021130242/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2008/06/theyre_chanting.html They're chanting his name...], ''The Boston Globe'', June 8, 2008.</ref> en route to a 108–102 Celtics victory.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080611083526/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280608002 Celts withstand Lakers' late Game 2 run behind Pierce, defense], ''Associated Press'', June 8, 2008.</ref><ref>Scott Tribble, [http://www.nba.com/celtics/playoffs2008/sidebar060808-powe-game2.html Celtics Build Lead with Heavy Dose of Powe-time] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080611230033/http://www.nba.com/celtics/playoffs2008/sidebar060808-powe-game2.html |date=June 11, 2008 }}, ''[[Boston Celtics|Celtics]].com'', June 9, 2008.</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/dailydime?page=dime-080609 Daily Dime: Powe steps up for Celtics], ''ESPN.com'', June 9, 2008.</ref>
[[Image:Leonpoweparade08.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Powe during the 2008 Boston Celtics championship parade.]]

===2008–09 NBA season===
On March 13, 2009, Powe started in place of the injured [[Kevin Garnett]], scoring a career-high 30 points, grabbing 11 rebounds and blocking a career-high 5 shots, in a 102–92 Celtics victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>[http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2009/03/14/powes_time_is_well_spent/ Powe's time is well spent] Boston Herald, March 14, 2009</ref>

Powe spent the end of the season attempting to recover from a right knee strain.  He returned in time for the playoffs, only to tear the ACL and meniscus in his left knee in Game 2 of the first round against the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2009/news/story?id=4086325 Leon Powe's postseason over: Boston Celtic has torn ACL - ESPN]</ref> Powe continued to play on the torn ACL for three minutes before being taken out. His season ended with the knee injury, and had successful surgery to repair the injury on May 5, 2009.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2009/playoffs2009/05/05/powe.surgery.update.ap/index.html Microfracture surgery on Powe's left knee a success] NBA.com, May 5, 2009</ref> On August 2, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] offered Powe an offer sheet worth two years and $1.8 million.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/fantasy/fantasy_playernews.jsp?date=08/02/2009&type=news NBA.com: Player News] NBA.com: Player News</ref> On August 11, 2009, Powe and the Cavaliers agreed in principle to the deal with an option on the second year.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4392457&campaign=rss&source=ESPNHeadlines Cavs, Leon Powe agreed two-year deal], ESPN.GO.com, August 11, 2009.</ref> On August 12, 2009, he officially signed the deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/powe_signed_090812.html |title=Cavaliers Sign Leon Powe |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=August 12, 2009 |access-date=August 12, 2009}}</ref>

===2010–11 NBA season===

On February 24, 2011, Powe was waived when the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] needed to clear their roster capacity after making two trades.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/trade_110224.html CAVALIERS: Cavaliers Acquire Erden and Harangody from Boston for Future Second Round Pick]</ref><ref name=grizzlies>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6184403 Free agent Leon Powe signed by Memphis Grizzlies - ESPN]</ref> He had just recovered from surgery to repair the torn meniscus in his right knee which had kept him sidelined for six weeks.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6000598 Cleveland Cavaliers' Leon Powe out 6 weeks after knee surgery - ESPN]</ref> Over a week later, Powe signed for the rest of the season with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref name=grizzlies/>

== Basketball post-career ==
In 2014, Powe was hired by the Celtics as community ambassador.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-09-30 |title=Celtics Hire Leon Powe For 'Whatever Danny (Ainge) Wants Me To Do' |url=https://nesn.com/2014/09/celtics-hire-leon-powe-for-whatever-danny-ainge-wants-me-to-do/ |access-date=2022-05-30 |website=NESN.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
